newsitem.title: CHINA: China to launch Apstar 2R satellite in late 1997.
newsitem.headline: China to launch Apstar 2R satellite in late 1997.

text.p: China will use a new-generation Long March 3B rocket to launch a communications satellite for a Hong Kong company later this year, officials said on Thursday.
The Apstar 2R satellite would be launched to replace Apstar 2, which was destroyed when its Long March carrier rocket blew up shortly after lift-off in January 1995, killing six people.
"We will launch the satellite after August," said Zhang Lihui, spokeswoman for the Chinese General Company of Astronautics Industry.
Apstar 2R was owned by the Beijing-controlled Hong Kong firm APT Satellite, Zhang said, but gave no further details.
China's space industry has been plagued by a string of failures recently.
In August 1996, a Long March 3 rocket failed to place the U.S.-made Chinasat-7 telecommunications satellite in its proper orbit.

In February of that year, a launch of a Long March 3B rocket ended in disaster when it exploded just seconds after lift-off, killing six people, injuring 57 and destroying its Intelsat satellite cargo.

China would try to boost the international market share of its Long March rocket by improving the reliability of the launcher, said Liu Jiyuan, general manager of the Chinese General Company of Astronautics Industry.
China also hoped to be able to make satellites for export by the year 2000, Liu was quoted as saying by the China News Service. It gave no further details.
